Definition: from ἀγγέλλω (probably derived from G71; compare G34) (to bring tidings); a messenger; especially an "angel"; by implication, a pastor:--angel, messenger.
BiblicalUsage: An angel is a messenger, and Scripture gives the word its widest work: the angel who announces Jesus' birth to Mary, the angels who minister to Him after the temptation, the angel who rolls the stone from the tomb, the angels who will gather the elect, and the fallen angels kept in chains. The same word names the herald of good news and the warrior of judgment.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe angels are real and busy, and the Bible never lets me treat them as decoration: they announce, they guard, they fight, and they will gather. I hold that God sends His messengers to His people still, and that the angels who stood at the empty tomb are the same kind of servants who watch over us now.
RelatedPeople: Mary, Mother of Jesus; Jesus; Gabriel
RelatedEvents: The Annunciation to Mary; The Temptation in the Wilderness
